Normalized metric variants to base forms and standardized naming conventions
Removed placeholder 'None' values since paper doesn't use LLM judges

guideline: Judges compared responses from our model vs baseline (GPT-2) based on answerability and semantics in single-turn settings
Judges evaluated complete multi-turn simulated conversations for overall quality between RL agent and user model
- Judges were asked to pick the better response based on criteria like answerability and semantics in single-turn settings, and to decide which conversation has higher quality in multi-turn settings.
Judges were asked to compare responses and select the better one based on answerability and semantics, and to evaluate whole multi-turn simulated conversations for overall quality.

In the first setting, we asked judges to pick the better response among the one generated by our model and a baseline model (Pre-Trained GPT2) based on various criteria like answerability and semantics. In the second setting, in case of multi-turn we used 200 simulated conversations between RL agent and a user model to judge the whole conversation for responses uttered by agent.

overall_notes: The extraction was generally accurate. Main improvements were normalizing metric names to base forms and removing criteria not explicitly mentioned. The paper focuses on dialogue generation with reinforcement learning and weak supervision for long-term conversation success.
